themes.name: Purine / nucleic-acid-associated
themes.description: Ring-breathing and imidazole modes of purine bases and their nucleic-acid context. The best-validated theme in GAIRA: adenine perturbation drives its own encoding component, and enzymatic urate depletion selectively removes a purine component.

contributing_components.interpretation: Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by purine chemistry (top analyte guanine). Perturbation-responsive in 4 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: xanthine, guanine, pyruvate.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by sterol chemistry (top analyte adenine). Perturbation-responsive in 7 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: hypoxanthine, adenine, acetoacetate.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by organic_acid chemistry (top analyte phosphoenolpyruvate). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: oleate, albumin, serine.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by pyrimidine chemistry (top analyte thymine). Perturbation-responsive in 7 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: hypoxanthine, adenine, phosphate.

themes.known_ambiguities: Purine sub-classes split into {adenine,hypoxanthine} and {xanthine,guanine}; a single axis cannot resolve them. Pyrimidines are a separate theme.
themes.domain_caveats: In serum, purine bands (adenine 725, hypoxanthine) are among the few reliably recovered because purines chemisorb strongly to Ag; elsewhere weaker.
component_caveats: c3: low chemical purity — the audit's coarse label is unreliable; trust the reference loadings and perturbation identity over the label.
c13: low chemical purity — the audit's coarse label is unreliable; trust the reference loadings and perturbation identity over the label.
c13: below-threshold bootstrap stability; may be partly a fitting mixture.

themes.name: Saccharide / glycan
themes.description: C-O/C-C stretching and C-O-C glycosidic modes of mono- and polysaccharides (glucose 1060/1120, glycogen). Several stable components contribute.

contributing_components.interpretation: Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by saccharide chemistry (top analyte (-)-arabinose). Perturbation-responsive in 4 dose experiment(s) (down). Serum-spike activators: albumin.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by saccharide chemistry (top analyte (+)-galactosamine). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (down). Serum-spike activators: oleate, albumin, serine.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by saccharide chemistry (top analyte (+)-dextrose). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (down). Serum-spike activators: albumin, oleate, guanine.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by polysaccharide chemistry (top analyte cellulose). Perturbation-responsive in 6 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: ergothioneine, urate, histidine.

themes.known_ambiguities: Monosaccharide isomers (glucose/fructose/galactose) share nearly identical fingerprint-region spectra; glycan branching is not resolved.
themes.domain_caveats: Serum glucose is millimolar; expect a large, non-specific saccharide signal.
component_caveats: c10: below-threshold bootstrap stability; may be partly a fitting mixture.

themes.name: Protein / peptide
themes.description: Amide I/III backbone modes and aromatic side-chain rings. The most mathematically stable motif family (c2 stability 0.965) and dominant in serum.

contributing_components.interpretation: Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by protein chemistry (top analyte superoxide dismutases). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: ergothioneine, oleate, xanthine.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by small_nitrogenous chemistry (top analyte urea). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: serine, oleate, riboflavin.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by protein chemistry (top analyte melanin). Perturbation-responsive in 6 dose experiment(s) (down). Serum-spike activators: urate, ascorbate, glucose.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by small_nitrogenous chemistry (top analyte creatinine). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: xanthine, guanine, oleate.

themes.known_ambiguities: Amide bands overlap lipid CH2 (1450) and aromatic amino-acid rings; the protein theme and aromatic-amino-acid theme share evidence.
themes.domain_caveats: Albumin dominates serum; a large protein signal is expected and non-specific.
component_caveats: c19: low chemical purity — the audit's coarse label is unreliable; trust the reference loadings and perturbation identity over the label.

themes.description: CH2 twisting (1300), CH2 scissoring (1440) and C=C (1650) of fatty-acyl chains in triacylglycerols, fatty acids and phospholipids. c1 (bands 1302, 1442) is the archetypal contributor.

contributing_components.interpretation: Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by triglyceride chemistry (top analyte elaidic acid). Perturbation-responsive in 4 dose experiment(s) (up).

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by fatty_acid chemistry (top analyte myristic acid). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: oleate, adenine, histidine.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by fatty_acid chemistry (top analyte arachidonic acid). Perturbation-responsive in 3 dose experiment(s) (down). Serum-spike activators: glycerol, leucine, urea.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by protein chemistry (top analyte melanin). Perturbation-responsive in 6 dose experiment(s) (down). Serum-spike activators: urate, ascorbate, glucose.

themes.known_ambiguities: Acyl-chain bands are shared across ALL lipid subclasses; the atlas resolves lipid CLASS but not species (saturated triacylglycerols are indistinguishable).
themes.domain_caveats: Serum lipoproteins carry a large, matrix-level acyl signal.
component_caveats: c7: low chemical purity — the audit's coarse label is unreliable; trust the reference loadings and perturbation identity over the label.

themes.name: Protein / peptide
themes.description: Amide I/III backbone modes and aromatic side-chain rings. The most mathematically stable motif family (c2 stability 0.965) and dominant in serum.

contributing_components.interpretation: Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by protein chemistry (top analyte superoxide dismutases). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: ergothioneine, oleate, xanthine.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by small_nitrogenous chemistry (top analyte urea). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: serine, oleate, riboflavin.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by protein chemistry (top analyte melanin). Perturbation-responsive in 6 dose experiment(s) (down). Serum-spike activators: urate, ascorbate, glucose.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by small_nitrogenous chemistry (top analyte creatinine). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: xanthine, guanine, oleate.

themes.known_ambiguities: Amide bands overlap lipid CH2 (1450) and aromatic amino-acid rings; the protein theme and aromatic-amino-acid theme share evidence.
themes.domain_caveats: Albumin dominates serum; a large protein signal is expected and non-specific.
component_caveats: c19: low chemical purity — the audit's coarse label is unreliable; trust the reference loadings and perturbation identity over the label.

themes.name: Purine / nucleic-acid-associated
themes.description: Ring-breathing and imidazole modes of purine bases and their nucleic-acid context. The best-validated theme in GAIRA: adenine perturbation drives its own encoding component, and enzymatic urate depletion selectively removes a purine component.

contributing_components.interpretation: Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by purine chemistry (top analyte guanine). Perturbation-responsive in 4 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: xanthine, guanine, pyruvate.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by sterol chemistry (top analyte adenine). Perturbation-responsive in 7 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: hypoxanthine, adenine, acetoacetate.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by organic_acid chemistry (top analyte phosphoenolpyruvate). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: oleate, albumin, serine.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by pyrimidine chemistry (top analyte thymine). Perturbation-responsive in 7 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: hypoxanthine, adenine, phosphate.

themes.known_ambiguities: Purine sub-classes split into {adenine,hypoxanthine} and {xanthine,guanine}; a single axis cannot resolve them. Pyrimidines are a separate theme.
themes.domain_caveats: In serum, purine bands (adenine 725, hypoxanthine) are among the few reliably recovered because purines chemisorb strongly to Ag; elsewhere weaker.
component_caveats: c3: low chemical purity — the audit's coarse label is unreliable; trust the reference loadings and perturbation identity over the label.
c13: low chemical purity — the audit's coarse label is unreliable; trust the reference loadings and perturbation identity over the label.
c13: below-threshold bootstrap stability; may be partly a fitting mixture.

themes.name: Saccharide / glycan
themes.description: C-O/C-C stretching and C-O-C glycosidic modes of mono- and polysaccharides (glucose 1060/1120, glycogen). Several stable components contribute.

contributing_components.interpretation: Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by saccharide chemistry (top analyte (-)-arabinose). Perturbation-responsive in 4 dose experiment(s) (down). Serum-spike activators: albumin.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by saccharide chemistry (top analyte (+)-galactosamine). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (down). Serum-spike activators: oleate, albumin, serine.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by saccharide chemistry (top analyte (+)-dextrose). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (down). Serum-spike activators: albumin, oleate, guanine.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by polysaccharide chemistry (top analyte cellulose). Perturbation-responsive in 6 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: ergothioneine, urate, histidine.

themes.known_ambiguities: Monosaccharide isomers (glucose/fructose/galactose) share nearly identical fingerprint-region spectra; glycan branching is not resolved.
themes.domain_caveats: Serum glucose is millimolar; expect a large, non-specific saccharide signal.
component_caveats: c10: below-threshold bootstrap stability; may be partly a fitting mixture.

themes.name: Organic acid / central metabolism
themes.description: Carboxylate symmetric stretch (~1400) and C-C skeletal modes of small central-metabolism acids (citrate, lactate, pyruvate, ascorbate).

contributing_components.interpretation: Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by organic_acid chemistry (top analyte phosphate). Perturbation-responsive in 6 dose experiment(s) (down). Serum-spike activators: oleate, albumin, arginine.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by organic_acid chemistry (top analyte phosphoenolpyruvate). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: oleate, albumin, serine.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by amino_acid chemistry (top analyte fumarate). Perturbation-responsive in 6 dose experiment(s) (down). Serum-spike activators: ergothioneine, urate, albumin.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by small_nitrogenous chemistry (top analyte urea). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: serine, oleate, riboflavin.

themes.known_ambiguities: The 1400 cm-1 carboxylate band is generic to many anions and to Ag-carboxylate adsorption; a strong 1400 signal is not specific to any one acid.
themes.domain_caveats: Ag-colloid adsorption itself produces carboxylate-like bands; treat with caution.
component_caveats: c14: low chemical purity — the audit's coarse label is unreliable; trust the reference loadings and perturbation identity over the label.
c22: low chemical purity — the audit's coarse label is unreliable; trust the reference loadings and perturbation identity over the label.
c22: below-threshold bootstrap stability; may be partly a fitting mixture.

themes.name: Sulfur / antioxidant
themes.description: C-S and S-H modes of thiol/thione antioxidants (glutathione, cysteine, ergothioneine). Ergothioneine perturbation drives components in this theme.

contributing_components.interpretation: Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by amino_acid chemistry (top analyte glycine). Perturbation-responsive in 6 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: ergothioneine, fructose, rna.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by small_nitrogenous chemistry (top analyte urea). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: serine, oleate, riboflavin.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by polysaccharide chemistry (top analyte cellulose). Perturbation-responsive in 6 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: ergothioneine, urate, histidine.

Latent Raman motif whose reference loadings are dominated by protein chemistry (top analyte superoxide dismutases). Perturbation-responsive in 5 dose experiment(s) (up/down). Serum-spike activators: ergothioneine, oleate, xanthine.

themes.known_ambiguities: Ergothioneine's encoding component (c19) is low-purity and generic; the sulfur theme is supported by perturbation but not by a clean atlas component.
themes.domain_caveats: Thione sulfur binds Ag strongly, so serum ergothioneine is one of the few recoverable cofactors.
component_caveats: c9: low chemical purity — the audit's coarse label is unreliable; trust the reference loadings and perturbation identity over the label.
c9: below-threshold bootstrap stability; may be partly a fitting mixture.

domain_interpretation.description: Pooled/patient serum via Ag-colloid SERS. Background-dominated (Spike Validation): only strong Ag adsorbers are reliably recovered.
domain_notes: nucleic_purine: elevated and reliably recovered in serum.
caveats: Albumin, cholesterol and glucose are millimolar and dominate; large signals in their themes are non-specific.
Weak Ag adsorbers (amino acids, most lipids) are poorly recovered; a LOW score does not mean the analyte is absent.
All serum SERS is out of domain for a Raman atlas; read with the OOD flag.

domain_interpretation.description: Pooled/patient serum via Ag-colloid SERS. Background-dominated (Spike Validation): only strong Ag adsorbers are reliably recovered.
domain_notes: nucleic_purine: elevated and reliably recovered in serum.
caveats: Albumin, cholesterol and glucose are millimolar and dominate; large signals in their themes are non-specific.
Weak Ag adsorbers (amino acids, most lipids) are poorly recovered; a LOW score does not mean the analyte is absent.
All serum SERS is out of domain for a Raman atlas; read with the OOD flag.
